question.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Netherlands, whose name literally means "low-lying countries"
question.text: Part of the modern-day Netherlands gained independence from the Spanish Empire in a war named for this many years, which is how long it lasted.

swap.leadin: This European country was the original home of the British king William of Orange.
swap.text: Name this country, which contains cities like The Hague, Rotterdam, and Amsterdam.
swap.clue: The Sea Beggars operated in this nation, and the Treaty of Nonsuch allied this nation with Great Britain.

question.leadin: This country's independence movement began after a performance of Auber's The Mute Girl of Portici.
question.text: Name this country, whose revolution William I of the Netherland's Ten Days' Campaign couldn't suppress. This country is home to both Walloon and Flemish-supporting movements.
question.answerHtml: Belgium [or the Kingdom of Belgium; or Konigreich Belgien; or Koninkrijk Belgie; or Royaume de Belgique]
question.clue: World War I fighting in this country included the first use of chlorine gas during the Battle of Ypres .

swap.text: During his reign, Mobutu renamed his capital city to Kinshasa. Previously, Kinshasa was named for this Belgian king who committed atrocities while he owned the Congo Free State.
swap.answerHtml: Leopold II of Belgium (prompt on Leopold or Leopoldville alone) (Kinshasa’s original name was Leopoldville)
swap.clue: Those lands had been gained for this man after he sent Henry Morton Stanley to negotiate with tribal chiefs.

question.leadin: Everyone knows the earth is flat, so why is it so hard to decide on a suitable map projection?
question.text: This projection, created in 1569, uses straight longitude and latitude lines that make Greenland and Africa nearly the same size.
question.clue: In 1569, this type of map projection was created by the namesake Flemish cartographer. A standard map projection, it is noted for distorting the size and shape of large objects, thus making Greenland look huge.

swap.leadin: This company was headed by a group known as the Heeren XVII ("seventeen").
swap.text: Name this company that controlled much of modern-day Indonesia from the settlement of Batavia. This company is considered one of the earliest mercantile corporations, and was rivals with a similar British company.
swap.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnieor VOC; prompt on East India Company]
swap.clue: Members of this group waterboarded and executed English merchants in the Amboyna massacre.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the career of Belgian prime minister Gaston Eyskens (AY-skens).
question.text: Eyskens hailed from this Dutch-speaking region in Belgium's north, which he governed alongside the French-speaking Wallonia.
question.clue: One ruler of this region was imprisoned with his two sons for attempting to ally with Edward Longshanks due to this region's prominence in the wool trade.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the military accomplishments of European dukes.
swap.text: The Duke of Alba established the "Council of Blood" during this war, the revolt of the Spanish Netherlands against Philip II of Spain.
swap.clue: Italian engineer Frederico Giambelli helped design fire ships during this war, during which Balthasar Gerard assassinated a leader.

question.text: This Flemish city saw half of its population flee in 1585 when the brutal "Spanish Fury" looted its besieged buildings and killed thousands of residents.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.text: Napoleon III denied a Hohenzollern prince with this name the chance to ascend to the Spanish throne, precipitating the Franco-Prussian War. A man with this name was crowned king of a new country after an 1830 revolution that broke out at an opera performance.
swap.clue: Atrocities committed under a king of this name were detailed in the Casement Report which included accounts of his Force Publique severing the limbs of workers who failed to meet rubber quotas.

question.leadin: Answer the following about The Hague.
question.text: This city in South Holland is best known for being besieged by the Spanish during the Eighty Years' War, only to be relieved when dikes were cut, flooding the area and allowing ships to carry provisions. A famous European university was created in this city afterwards.
question.clue: Plants obtained from the Dutch East India Company were used in the botanical garden at the university in this city, established in 1575. Rembrandt was born in this city.

swap.leadin: According to the book The Bookshop of the World, during this period, 10 times more books were produced per capita than in France or Spain.
swap.text: Name this period, also the subject of Simon Schama's The Embarrassment of Riches. This period's end is traditionally dated to the "Disaster Year" of 1672.
swap.answerHtml: Dutch Golden Age [or Gouden Eeuw; or Netherlands Golden Age; or Dutch Miracle; prompt on Golden Age]

question.leadin: After this meeting, Hugo Grotius was sentenced to life imprisonment, but escaped thanks to his mistress smuggling him out of prison in a book chest.
question.text: Name this 1618 to 1619 synod in the Netherlands convened to settle the Arminian controversy. This meeting saw disputes between the Arminians and followers of Franciscus Gomarus, as well as the condemnation of Johan von Oldenbarnevelt.
question.answerHtml: Synod of Dort [or Synod of Dordt or Synod of Dordrecht]
question.clue: Moderated by Bogerman, it set forth the doctrines of perseverance of saints, irresistible grace, total depravity, limited atonement, and unconditional election.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the colonial rivalry between the Dutch and the Portuguese.
swap.text: John Maurice governed this colony from Recife for much of its time under Dutch rule. The Dutch had earlier failed to hold Salvador after briefly capturing it.

question.text: This failed September 1944 operation, the largest airborne operation at the time, was an attempt by the Allies to end the war by moving through the Netherlands into Germany.
question.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

swap.text: This woman was the queen of the Netherlands during the war. She fled to Great Britain during the occupation and broadcast messages of inspiration to the Dutch resistance movement.

question.leadin: This man authored tracts like Defenso Fidei and De Imperio where he argued for the right of Holland to determine its own religious affairs.
question.text: Identify this "Miracle of Holland" who escaped from a life sentence at Loevestein after his wife smuggled him out of captivity in a book chest.
question.clue: This lawyer was tried alongside van Oldenbarnevelt for expressing tolerance toward the Arminians. This author of the international law book Mare Liberum escaped Loevestein ("LOO-vuh-stain") Castle while hidden in a book chest.

swap.text: Ludvigsen was influenced by the Provo movement, which passed urbanist "White Plans" in this non-Danish city. This city's own squatters movement was involved in its 1980 coronation riots.
swap.clue: A failed 1650 attack on this city, where wealthy regents like the Bicker brothers held power, preceded a 22-year vacancy of leadership ending in the "Disaster Year."

question.leadin: Since their pay had been confiscated by Elizabeth I en route to them, angry Spanish tercios decided to carry out this action as a way of compensating themselves for their lost wages.
question.text: Name this 1576 action, sometimes called the Spanish Fury, in which forces under Sancho d'Avila pillaged a wealthy port city for three days straight. Rather than breaking the will of the revolting Dutch, this event instead strengthened their resolve.
question.clue: Otto Oberstein, drowned in the Scheldt while retreating from it, and the five thousand troops under the Marquis de Havre mostly failed to offer any resistance.

swap.leadin: He was killed by Balthasar Gerard in what was probably the first assassination of a head of state with a gun.
swap.text: Name this Dutch stadtholder and Prince of Orange who led the Dutch revolt against Spanish control.
swap.answerHtml: William the Silent [or William I; or William of Orange]
swap.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.
